announcements.title: Stop babysitting one agent. Command a fleet.
announcements.body: Here's how to think about AgentWire: it's a self-hosted, keyboard-driven cockpit for running a whole fleet of Claude Code agents at once — not a voice toy with sessions bolted on. The capabilities compound. Every session is a window (F3 collage, Tab to cycle); the command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) runs any action; worktree sessions isolate parallel work; the scheduler runs recurring jobs unattended as draft PRs. Voice is a layer that stacks on all of it — push-to-talk in, spoken summaries by ear while you're off-tab, and global macOS hotkeys to dictate to a background session from any app. One person commands many agents instead of babysitting one.
highlights: From a wall of tmux panes to one cockpit — the pieces compound
Every session is a window: F3 collage, Tab to cycle, Cmd/Ctrl+K for any action
Worktrees + scheduler + council run parallel and unattended work
Voice is a compounding layer, not the headline

announcements.title: Press F1 — there's more than you think
announcements.body: AgentWire has a pile of keyboard shortcuts and features that were easy to miss. Now there's one place to see them all: press F1 (or ?) anytime for a cheat sheet of every shortcut, plus a quick tour of features worth knowing — council, push-to-talk, window collage, worktrees, scratchpad, and more. There's also a ? button in the sidebar header if you'd rather click.
highlights: F1 or ? — keyboard shortcut cheat sheet, from anywhere
Doubles as a feature tour: discover what you're not using yet
Also in the sidebar header (?) and the command palette

announcements.title: Parallel agents, each on their own branch
announcements.body: Worktree sessions are now a first-class primitive. `agentwire worktree <name>` spins up an isolated git worktree on a fresh branch with its own standalone session — so you can fan out several autonomous agents at once without them stepping on each other. The base branch is derived from your repo (no hardcoded main), names follow templates, monorepos work, and a local branch↔session registry lets you list, remove, and prune them. Best part: each session knows its own etiquette. The spawn verb sets the posture, so a worktree agent automatically gets the isolation / verify-in-worktree / draft-PR / notify-back safety contract — your first prompt only needs the task.
highlights: agentwire worktree <name> — isolated branch + worktree + standalone session
Repo-derived base branch, naming templates, monorepo support
Etiquette comes from the spawn verb — agents self-isolate and report back

announcements.title: Terminal sizing now respects your tmux config
announcements.body: Until now, resizing the portal terminal silently forced the whole tmux window to the browser's size — pinning it into manual mode and breaking your window-size setting (largest/smallest/latest) for every connected terminal. Fixed: the portal now behaves like any other tmux client, your policy decides, and previously stuck windows heal automatically when you open them in the portal. If you liked 'the browser always wins', set window-size latest in ~/.tmux.conf. Tip: window-size smallest keeps sessions fully visible even on a phone or tablet.
highlights: Your window-size policy works again — for every client
Stuck windows self-heal on portal attach (agentwire resize works too)
On a tablet? Try: set -g window-size smallest

announcements.title: You're an early one
announcements.body: AgentWire is young and shaped by the handful of people running it. Bug, idea, or just hello — open an issue, it's read.

announcements.title: New idea? Cmd+K and go.
announcements.body: AgentWire can now spin up a whole project from a single sentence. Press Cmd/Ctrl+K (or the New idea button), type — or speak — what you want to build, and it scaffolds the folder, starts an agent, and hands it your idea as the first message. You watch it get to work the moment the window opens.
highlights: Idea-first capture — type an idea, get a running agent
Instant voice mode — browser speech in and out, zero setup
